title: The flags after an add
description:
Write `add8(a, b)`, which simulates the instruction `add al, bl` on two bytes and returns the 8-bit result together with the four flags it sets:

- `zf`: the result is zero;
- `sf`: bit 7 of the result is set;
- `cf`: the true unsigned sum did not fit in 8 bits;
- `of`: the true **signed** sum (treating `a` and `b` as `std::int8_t`) did not fit in 8 bits.

Then write `sub8(a, b)` for `sub al, bl`. For subtraction, `cf` is set when `b` is larger than `a` as unsigned numbers (a borrow), and `of` when the true signed difference does not fit.

```
add8(127, 1)  -> result 0x80, sf, of
add8(255, 1)  -> result 0,    zf, cf
sub8(3, 5)    -> result 0xFE, sf, cf
```
hints: Work out the true answers in a wider type, where nothing overflows: once with the bytes as unsigned (0 to 255) and once as signed (-128 to 127).
The result is the low 8 bits of either true answer (they are the same bits). CF says whether the unsigned true answer is outside 0 to 255; OF whether the signed one is outside -128 to 127.
